## Solution

The functor $\Pi|\mathcal{O}:\mathcal{O}\to\mathcal{GP}$ is the restriction of the **fundamental groupoid functor** $\Pi$ to the category $\mathcal{O}$.

### The fundamental groupoid functor $\Pi$

For any topological space $Y$, the **fundamental groupoid** $\Pi(Y)$ is the groupoid defined by:

- **Objects of $\Pi(Y)$**: the points of $Y$, i.e. $\mathrm{Ob}(\Pi(Y)) = Y$.
- **Morphisms of $\Pi(Y)$**: homotopy classes (relative to endpoints) of paths in $Y$. That is, for $x,y\in Y$, the set of arrows $\mathrm{Hom}_{\Pi(Y)}(x,y)$ is the set of path-homotopy classes $[\gamma]$ of paths $\gamma:[0,1]\to Y$ with $\gamma(0)=x$ and $\gamma(1)=y$.
- **Composition**: concatenation of paths (well-defined on homotopy classes).
- **Identity** at $x$: the class of the constant path at $x$.
- **Inverse** of $[\gamma]$: the class of the reversed path $\bar\gamma(t)=\gamma(1-t)$.

This is a groupoid (every morphism is invertible) because every path class $[\gamma]$ has inverse $[\bar\gamma]$.

For a continuous map $f:Y\to Z$, the induced functor $\Pi(f):\Pi(Y)\to\Pi(Z)$ sends a point $x\mapsto f(x)$ and a path class $[\gamma]\mapsto[f\circ\gamma]$. This makes $\Pi$ a functor $\mathbf{Top}\to\mathcal{GP}$.

### Restriction to $\mathcal{O}$

The category $\mathcal{O}$ is the poset category of (open) subsets of $X$ ordered by inclusion. An object of $\mathcal{O}$ is a subset $U\subseteq X$, and a morphism $U\to V$ is the inclusion $i_{U,V}:U\hookrightarrow V$ whenever $U\subseteq V$.

The restricted functor $\Pi|\mathcal{O}:\mathcal{O}\to\mathcal{GP}$ acts as follows:

- **On objects**: each object $U\in\mathcal{O}$ (a subset of $X$) is sent to its fundamental groupoid
$$\Pi|\mathcal{O}(U) \;=\; \Pi(U),$$
  the fundamental groupoid of the subspace $U$. Concretely:
  - **Objects of $\Pi(U)$**: the points of $U$.
  - **Morphisms of $\Pi(U)$**: homotopy classes (rel endpoints) of paths lying entirely in $U$.

- **On morphisms**: each inclusion $i_{U,V}:U\hookrightarrow V$ (with $U\subseteq V$) is sent to the induced functor
$$\Pi(i_{U,V}):\Pi(U)\longrightarrow\Pi(V),$$
  which sends a point $x\in U$ to the same point $x\in V$, and a path class $[\gamma]$ in $U$ to the class $[i_{U,V}\circ\gamma]$ of the same path regarded as a path in $V$ (since $U\subseteq V$, every path in $U$ is automatically a path in $V$).

### Conclusion

Under the functor $\Pi|\mathcal{O}:\mathcal{O}\to\mathcal{GP}$, **each object $U$ of $\mathcal{O}$ — that is, each (open) subset $U\subseteq X$ — is mapped to its fundamental groupoid $\Pi(U)$**, whose objects are the points of $U$ and whose morphisms are homotopy classes of paths in $U$. Inclusion morphisms $U\hookrightarrow V$ are mapped to the evident inclusion-of-groupoids functors $\Pi(U)\to\Pi(V)$ induced by regarding paths in $U$ as paths in the larger space $V$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
